methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia's AI challenge isn't data centers. It's small-business adoption | Guest column - Richmond Times-Dispatch
signals.signal_reading: Opinion piece explicitly diagnoses the real challenge: AI capability concentrating in data center infrastructure rather than distributed small-business adoption, confirming the shallow/concentrated trajectory unless intentional distribution efforts occur.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Young workforce feeling 'pressure' from AI suggests anxiety without adequate skill-building infrastructure—a hallmark of shallow engagement where AI is perceived as threat rather than tool due to lack of deep capability development.

signals.title: University of Virginia Students Help Businesses Explore AI - govtech.com
signals.signal_reading: UVA students helping businesses explore AI represents peer-to-peer capability transfer and hands-on learning—exactly the distributed knowledge-building mechanism that could activate deeper adoption beyond metro centers if scaled statewide.

signals.title: Norfolk looks to add AI dispatcher tool for non-emergency calls - WAVY.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk deploying turnkey AI dispatcher tool for non-emergency calls exemplifies shallow platform adoption—municipal capacity building through vendor solutions rather than indigenous technical development, spreading use without deepening local expertise.

signals.title: Roanoke citizens question potential data center plans in potential land development - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Community resistance to data center development in Roanoke signals that infrastructure investment alone doesn't distribute capability—physical presence of AI infrastructure may concentrate economic benefit while leaving local population without skill access or agency.
